implementation_notes: The default C++ realization: the interface header contains only an abstract class with pure virtual functions and a virtual destructor; a factory declared in the same header is defined in the implementation library, so clients link the contract and never see the implementation class. Virtual dispatch costs one indirection per call; use this form when implementations are chosen at run time.
pitfalls: A pure abstract class without a virtual destructor leaks (or is undefined behaviour) when an object is deleted through the base pointer.
The vtable is ABI-fragile: adding or reordering virtual functions breaks binary compatibility for clients compiled against an older header.

Returning std::unique_ptr<Clock> requires the complete type only in the implementation file; declaring the factory's return type with an incomplete type in client code is fine, but deleting a raw base pointer is not.

variants.name: Pimpl compile firewall
variants.implementation_notes: The ABI-stable reading of the pattern (Core Guidelines I.27, cppreference): the public class in the header holds only an opaque pointer to an implementation class defined in the .cpp, so private data and implementation details are removed from the object representation and clients recompile only when the public interface changes. Choose pimpl over pure virtual interfaces when there is exactly one implementation but a stable ABI or fast rebuilds matter.
pitfalls: std::unique_ptr<impl> needs the complete type wherever the deleter is instantiated: the destructor and move operations must be user-declared and defined in the .cpp.
A const member function forwarding through a non-const pointer calls the non-const overload; wrap the pointer in std::experimental::propagate_const or write both overloads.
Every call pays an extra indirection and every object an extra allocation; in hot paths or for small value-like types this can dominate.
